traditional: A hard contact. Communication, commerce, and contracts works against action, conflict, and heat - obstruction, friction, and strained outcomes in these areas.
modern: Mind meets drive. A sharp, restless intellect that attacks problems rather than mulling them, and doesn't shy from debate. Psychologically the square is inner tension to integrate: Arguments and verbal aggression; the mind never switches off. The growth is owning both sides instead of splitting them.

cyclic.waxing: Crisis of action: take conscious hold and build a durable form for thinking against drive, or be thrown off course.
cyclic.waning: Crisis of meaning: break down the thinking/drive form that has outlived its purpose and reorient toward the next cycle.

business: Friction in this area. Fast, cutting thinking; the task is channeling the edge productively.
shadow: Scattered overthinking collides with anger and recklessness; forcing or splitting it instead of working it through.
arcApplying: Friction builds toward a forced adjustment.
arcSeparating: The crisis passes; what was restructured settles.

readerCopy.summary: One sharp reply can turn a practical disagreement into the argument you spend the rest of the day regretting.
readerCopy.body: One sharp reply can turn a practical disagreement into the argument you spend the rest of the day regretting. When Mercury squares Mars, thought and anger grind against each other, making impatience easier to hear in your words and disagreement easier to interpret as disrespect. The issue may genuinely need confronting, but irritation is likely to make the sentence harsher than the solution requires. Draft the scorched-earth response in a private document to clear your nervous system. Then, edit it down to the cold, professional facts and send the version that actually secures your objective.
